statement: Let $R$ be a ring, $M=F_0M\supset F_1M\supset\cdots$ a filtered $R$-module, $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, and $I=(f)$. Put $G_nM=\sum_{i=0}^n I^iF_{n-i}M$ and $X=\operatorname{gr}_F M$. If the canonical graded surjection \[ \psi:(X/IX)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\longrightarrow \operatorname{gr}_G M, \qquad [m]T^\alpha\longmapsto[f^\alpha m] \] is an isomorphism, then $f$ is $X$-quasi-regular. Here $[m]\in X_p$ and $T^\alpha$ has degree $|\alpha|$, so the target degree is $p+|\alpha|$. No separatedness assumption is needed. This is the final printed IV 19.5.5(b)$\Rightarrow$(c), pp.~206--209; the footnote on p.~207 explicitly credits Deligne's proof. The corresponding numbers in $0_{\rm IV}$, p.~94, are a different remark and a proof of Theorem 19.5.3, not the claims criticized in this letter.

statement: The final 1967 text, p.~209, assumes only that the $f_i$ have no homogeneous component of degree zero. Under that wording its quasi-regular$\Rightarrow$regular assertion is false. It is not an ordinary regular sequence. A valid corrected statement is obtained by requiring the $f_i$ to be homogeneous of positive degree; more generally the exact sufficient hypothesis is separatedness of each successive quotient for the $I$-adic topology, as in $0_{\rm IV}$ 15.1.9.

If $E$ is cocomplete, condition (3) may omit the last, slice-filteredness condition. In that case it also suffices that $E$ have a small dense subcategory of $\kappa$-presentable objects.

statement: Let $P$ be an $A$-module. It is a differential if and only if \[ d_1d_0=0\quad\hbox{and}\quad d_2d_1=0, \qquad d_2=d|_{\Lambda_A^2P}. \] The first equation alone is insufficient, even for a free module of rank three over $\mathbf Q$.

statement: Let $F=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}c_\alpha X^\alpha$ over $U=\mathbf Z[c_\alpha]$, in $N\geq1$ variables. With the resultant normalized by $\operatorname{Res}(X_1^{e_1},\ldots,X_N^{e_N})=1$, put \[ a(N,d)=\frac{(d-1)^N-(-1)^N}{d},\qquad D=N(d-1)^{N-1},\qquad w=d(d-1)^{N-1}. \] There is a primitive integral polynomial $\operatorname{Disc}_{N,d}\in U$ such that \[ \operatorname{Res}(\partial_1F,\ldots,\partial_NF) =d^{a(N,d)}\operatorname{Disc}_{N,d}(F). \] It has degree $D$ in the coefficients, and $\operatorname{Disc}_{N,d}(F\circ g)=\det(g)^w\operatorname{Disc}_{N,d}(F)$. Over any field, its vanishing is equivalent to the existence, after a finite field extension, of a nonzero common zero of $F,\partial_1F,\ldots,\partial_NF$.

statement: Let $S$ be any scheme, $E$ locally free of rank $N$, and $M\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^d E$ an invertible subbundle. There is a canonical section \[ \delta_X\in \Gamma\bigl(S,M^{-D}\otimes(\det E)^{\otimes w}\bigr). \] Its formation commutes with arbitrary base change, and $X\to S$ is smooth if and only if $\delta_X$ generates this line bundle at every point of $S$. statement: For $f=ax^2+by^2+cz^2+dxy+exz+f_0yz$ the divided discriminant is \[ 4abc-af_0^2-be^2-cd^2+def_0. \] It is one half of the integral Hessian determinant, not the Hessian determinant itself. Over $\mathbf F_2$, $x^2+yz$ defines a smooth conic: its derivatives are $0,z,y$, and a critical projective point would have $y=z=0$, where the equation forces $x=0$. Its divided discriminant is $1$, while the naive resultant of derivatives is $0$. The program \texttt{code/geometry\_discriminant.py} computes the integral formula and checks that the singular-locus ideal on each of the three standard affine charts has Gr\"obner basis $\{1\}$ over $\mathbf F_2$. Thus it checks emptiness over every field extension, not merely absence of $\mathbf F_2$-points.

In cote 23/005, $\det E\simeq L^5$ and $M\simeq L^6$, so the corrected discriminant line is \[ M^{-12}\otimes(\det E)^{12}\simeq L^{-12}. \] The adjunction formula on that page identifies the Hodge line with $L^{-1}$; hence this is its twelfth tensor power. statement: Over $\mathbf Q$, take $d=1$ and assign the full formal coordinate torsor $\mathcal F_\infty(X/T)=\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n(X/T)$. It is an affine $X$-scheme, locally an infinite polynomial extension of $\mathbf G_m$; its construction commutes with base change and \'{e}tale pullback. Thus it is a cartesian section of the type allowed on 23/040. It is not of finite order. For every $n\geq1$ the map $t\mapsto t+t^{n+1}$ is \'{e}tale on a neighbourhood of zero and has the identity $n$-jet, but acts nontrivially on formal frames (already on their $(n+1)$st jet). This directly violates $n$-locality for every $n$. Its fibre has infinitely many algebraically independent coordinate coefficients, so it is not finitely presented. The coefficient calculation for orders $1$ through $8$ is checked in \texttt{code/geometry\_finite\_checks.py}; the displayed coefficient $t^{n+1}$ proves the assertion for every $n$. A uniform order also needs a global boundedness condition on the base. On $S=\coprod_{m\geq1}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$, prescribe the order-$m$ frame torsor on the $m$th component. Its values are locally of finite presentation and formally local; no single $n$ works on all components. This does not contradict the quasi-compact-base theorem.

statement: Take $\mathcal M=B(\ell^2(\mathbf N))$ with its usual trace and let $P$ be a rank-one projection. Set $A=1-\tfrac12P$ and $B=1+P$. These are positive invertible operators in $1+\mathcal J$, and $AB=1$. The decreasing rearrangement $\mu_t(A)$ is identically $1$: infinitely many singular values are $1$, and the single value $1/2$ is invisible to this rearrangement. For $B$, $\mu_t(B)=2$ on $0\leq t<1$ and is $1$ thereafter. Consequently \[ e^{\int_0^\infty\log\mu_t(A)\,dt}=1,\quad e^{\int_0^\infty\log\mu_t(B)\,dt}=2,\quad e^{\int_0^\infty\log\mu_t(AB)\,dt}=1. \] Thus the literal proposed formula is false already for invertible finite-rank perturbations of $1$. The finite matrix block is verified by \texttt{code/geometry\_determinant\_checks.py}; the infinite identity tail explains why finite truncations of the \emph{rearrangement} do not compute the same invariant. The spectral-trace determinant instead gives $1/2$, $2$, and $1$, respectively.

statement: For $A\in\mathcal D$ define \[ \Delta_\tau(A)=\exp\bigl(\tau(\log|A|)\bigr),\qquad e^{-\infty}=0. \] The positive part of $\log|A|$ is trace integrable, so this is unambiguously in $[0,\infty)$. For all $A,B\in\mathcal D$, including noninvertible ones, \[ \Delta_\tau(AB)=\Delta_\tau(A)\Delta_\tau(B),\qquad \Delta_\tau(A^*)=\Delta_\tau(A). \] It follows that, for $H=A^*A$, \[ \Delta_\tau(B^*HB) =\Delta_\tau(A^*A)\Delta_\tau(B^*B). \] When $\tau(1)<\infty$, these statements hold for every $A,B\in\mathcal M$.

If $D\geq0$, $D-1\in\mathcal J$, and $\ell(D)>-\infty$, then \[ \lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0} \ell\left(\frac{C+\epsilon D}{1+\epsilon}\right)=\ell(C). \] In particular this holds for $D=1$.

statement: On $\ell^2$, the positive operators $2\,1$ and $\tfrac12\,1$ have trace-log determinants $+\infty$ and $0$. Their product has determinant $1$. There is no multiplication law with ordinary extended nonnegative numbers that assigns a definite value to $0\cdot\infty$ and makes all such examples consistent: replacing the second operator by $\tfrac14\,1$ makes the product determinant $0$, while the same two determinant values occur. Replacing it by $\tfrac34\,1$ makes the product determinant $+\infty$. Moreover $2\,1-2P$ has an infinite positive logarithmic integral and an infinite negative one, so its unregularized trace logarithm is undefined. Thus the all-$\lambda$ demand in H.2, with no domain qualification, is false or undefined, rather than a missing extension of Theorem~\ref{geo-H-determinant}.

statement: In the diffuse finite algebra $L^\infty([0,1])$ with integral trace, let $a_n=e^{-n}$ on $[0,1/n]$ and $a_n=1$ elsewhere. Then $\|a_n-1\|_1=(1-e^{-n})/n\to0$, but $\Delta(a_n)=e^{-1}\ne\Delta(1)$. Trace-norm continuity, proposed in the supplied study as an extension argument, is false, even for invertible approximants. The upper semicontinuity and special regularization actually proved above are what is needed. Also $B=-\operatorname{diag}(1/(2n))$ is compact but not trace class, $1+B>0$, and $\sum_n\log(1-1/(2n))=-\infty$. Its spectral determinant is $0$, which is finite. Hence ``finite determinant if and only if the compact perturbation is trace class'' is false when finite includes zero. Finally, if $B=UL$ is a polar decomposition, then $B^*HB=L U^*HU L$, not $LHL$. Dropping the conjugating $U$ would assume part of the multiplicativity being proved. These distinctions are required by sheets 28--30.

statement: For a connected scheme $X$ with geometric point $\bar x$ and a finite constant group $G$, its $G$-torsors are classified by continuous homomorphisms $\pi_1^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\bar x)\to G$ modulo conjugacy. A chosen point of the torsor above $\bar x$ removes conjugacy. For a ring $R$ of characteristic $p$ one instead has \[ H^1_{\mathrm{fppf}}(\operatorname{Spec}R,\alpha_p)=R/R^p. \] Thus ``finite'' cannot silently be replaced by ``finite \'etale''.
notes: Known classification and proved inseparable correction; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Every rank $n$ vector bundle on $\mathbf P^1_k$, for any field $k$, is $\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathcal O(a_i)$, with its integers determined up to permutation. Over an arbitrary affine base $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the complete classification is instead the groupoid of triples \[ (P_0,P_\infty,\phi),\qquad \phi:P_0\otimes_{R[t]}R[t,t^{-1}] \xrightarrow{\sim}P_\infty\otimes_{R[t^{-1}]}R[t,t^{-1}], \] where the two modules are finitely generated projective of rank $n$; morphisms are pairs of module isomorphisms intertwining $\phi$. For general $Y$, these data are descended along an affine open covering. Principal $\mathrm{GL}_n$-bundles have exactly this classification.
notes: Proved: field classification and exact relative replacement; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: On $\mathbf P^1_k\times\mathbf A^1_k$ take the extension $0\to\mathcal O(-1)\to E\to\mathcal O(1)\to0$ whose class is the coordinate $s$ in $H^1(\mathbf P^1,\mathcal O(-2))\otimes_k k[s]\simeq k[s]$. At $s=0$ it is $\mathcal O(-1)\oplus\mathcal O(1)$. At a nonzero field-valued point the boundary map after twisting by $-1$ is multiplication by $s$ from $H^0(\mathcal O)$ to $H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$. Consequently $H^0(E(-1))=0$, and the field classification with degree zero forces $E\simeq\mathcal O^2$. This is the precise obstruction behind treating (h) as just a list of integers independent of the base. The extension is locally free because it is an extension of locally free sheaves.
notes: Refuted: a relative bundle has constant splitting type; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Let $A_0/k$ be an abelian variety of dimension $g$, and let $W$ be a complete local noetherian ring with residue field $k$. On local Artinian $W$-algebras with residue field identified with $k$, the functor of abelian schemes equipped with an identification of their special fibre with $A_0$ is prorepresented by \[ W[[t_{11},t_{12},\ldots,t_{gg}]]. \] In particular, it is formally smooth over $W$, of relative tangent dimension $g^2$. No polarization is part of this deformation problem.
notes: Known, with all characteristics and the base specified; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Let $p:A\to S$ be an abelian scheme with zero section $e$, let $L$ be an invertible sheaf, and let $x,y\in A(S)$. Then \begin{align*} t_{x+y}^*L\otimes(t_x^*L)^{-1}\otimes(t_y^*L)^{-1}\otimes L \simeq p^*\bigl((x+y)^*L\otimes(x^*L)^{-1} \otimes(y^*L)^{-1}\otimes e^*L\bigr). \end{align*} Thus $x\mapsto[t_x^*L\otimes L^{-1}]$ is a homomorphism into the relative Picard functor. Neither this assertion nor its proof requires projectivity.
notes: Proved from the nonprojective cube theorem; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Let $S$ be a complex elliptic curve $E$, take $A=E\times S$, let $L=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal O_E(0)$, and take $x=y$ to be the diagonal section. The base line bundle in Theorem~\ref{geo-Kj} has degree $4-1-1=2$, and is nontrivial. Its pullback to $A$ is nontrivial because the zero section pulls it back to itself. Thus the absolute equality in $\operatorname{Pic}(A)$ without that base factor is false even for a projective constant family. Over a field the factor is a one-dimensional vector space and becomes trivial as a line bundle, which explains the usual field-valued formulation.
notes: Refuted: suppressing the base line bundle; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: If $S$ is formally smooth over $R$, then $\Omega_{S/R}$ is projective over $S$. An $R$-algebra retract of a formally smooth $R$-algebra is formally smooth over $R$.
notes: Proved: two lifting consequences; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Let $R$ be a ring, $t\in R$, and assume $\bigcap_{N\geq0}t^NR=0$. Every projective $R$-module $P$ satisfies $\bigcap_{N\geq0}t^NP=0$.
notes: Proved: a separation obstruction; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: For every field $K$ of characteristic zero, the element $f=\sum_{m\geq0}t^m/m!$ of $K[[t]]$ is transcendental over $K(t)$.
notes: Proved: the formal exponential is transcendental; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Let $k\subset K$ be fields of characteristic zero, let $n\geq1$, and put $A=K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$. The ordinary $A$-module $\Omega_{A/k}$ is not projective, and therefore is not free. Consequently $A$ is not formally smooth over $k$ for the discrete topology. In particular this holds for $\mathbf Q[[t]]/\mathbf Q$ and for every case of A.1 with finite-dimensional $\Omega_{K/k}$.
notes: Proved: A.1, with no restriction on $\Omega_{K/k}$; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: This proves the positive-dimensional presumption of cote 22/023 without assuming finite transcendence degree of $K/k$. The two supplied witnesses give either $\dim A>0$ or a doubtful $\dim A\geq0$. If the latter includes $n=0$, that reading is false: every characteristic-zero field extension is formally smooth and its differentials form a free vector space \cite[Tag 031U, Proposition 10.158.9]{rootStacksFields}. The same-field non-smoothness assertion is located by secondary literature at Matsumura, \emph{Commutative Ring Theory}, p.~215; that page has not yet been opened, so we rely on the complete proof above and make no novelty claim.
notes: Scope and source reading; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Let $k\subset K$ be fields of any characteristic and assume $\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}$ is infinite. For every $n\geq1$ the module $\Omega_{K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/k}$ is not projective.
notes: Proved: infinitely many coefficient differentials; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Let $k\subset K$ have characteristic $p>0$, and suppose $[kK^p:K^p]$ is infinite. Then $\Omega_{K[[t]]/k}$ contains a nonzero element in $\bigcap_{N\geq0}t^N\Omega_{K[[t]]/k}$.
notes: Proved: the Frobenius coefficient obstruction; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Let $k\subset K$ be fields of characteristic $p>0$ and let $n\geq1$. The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ is formally smooth over $k$ for the discrete topology. \item $K/k$ is separable and $[K:K^p]<\infty$. \end{enumerate} If (2) holds and a $p$-basis $c_1,\ldots,c_r$ of $k$ extends to a $p$-basis $c_1,\ldots,c_r,b_1,\ldots,b_s$ of $K$, then $\Omega_{K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/k}$ is free on $db_1,\ldots,db_s,dt_1,\ldots,dt_n$.
notes: Proved: A.2, exact criterion; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: The assertion on cote 22/022 that a finite $p$-basis of $K/k$ always extends by the $t_i$ to a $p$-basis of $K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/k$ is false if arbitrary imperfect $k$ is allowed. Take $k=K=\mathbf F_p(s_1,s_2,\ldots)$, where the $s_i$ are algebraically independent. The relative $p$-basis is empty, but for $n\geq1$ the power series ring is not formally smooth over $k$. If $k$ is perfect and $K/k$ is separable, the manuscript's finite-relative-$p$-basis criterion is correct, and the infinite case has a negative answer.
notes: Refuted: finite relative $p$-basis without a perfect base; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Let $R\to B$ be a map of noetherian rings, give $R$ the discrete topology and $B$ the $J$-adic topology, and suppose it is formally smooth for these topologies. For every $n\geq1$, put $B_n=B/J^n$. Then \[ L_{B/R}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B_n \simeq(\Omega_{B/R}\otimes_B B_n)[0], \qquad \Omega_{B/R}\otimes_B B_n\text{ is projective over }B_n. \] No finite generation of this projective module is asserted.
notes: Proved: the cotangent complex on each adic quotient; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Under Lemma~\ref{SA23-A-14}, assume $B$ is separated and complete for its $J$-adic topology. For every finite $B$-module $N$, \[ \operatorname{Ext}^i_B(L_{B/R},N)=0\qquad(i>0). \]
notes: Proved: vanishing with complete finite coefficients; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Let $A\twoheadrightarrow A_0$ be a surjection of noetherian rings with kernel $I$, where $I^2=0$. Let $A_0\to B_0$ be a noetherian algebra, separated and complete for a $J$-adic topology, formally smooth over the discrete ring $A_0$. Then there is a noetherian $A$-algebra $B$, flat over $A$, with an identification $B/IB\simeq B_0$. For the inverse image $\widetilde J$ of $J$, $B$ is separated, complete and formally smooth over $A$. Thus it is a Cohen lift in the draft's sense. The lift with its specified reduction is unique up to an $A$-isomorphism inducing the identity on $B_0$. Its automorphisms inducing that identity are the additive group \[ \operatorname{Der}_{A_0}(B_0,I\otimes_{A_0}B_0). \] Uniqueness of an isomorphism is not asserted.
notes: Proved: general noetherian adic Cohen lifting; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: EGA $0_{\rm IV}$ 19.7.2, printed pp.~108--109, proves the complete-local case with no separability restriction on residue extensions; Remark 19.7.3 distinguishes a different, noncomplete local lifting question. P\'erez Rodr\'iguez \cite[Corollary 4.3]{rootPerez2008} proves existence for affine smooth formal schemes, where smoothness includes pseudo finite type (Definition 1.3). Neither opened result alone gives the draft's full nonlocal adic assertion. Our proof combines the cotangent obstruction theorem with a calculation on every adic quotient. It does not assert a lift for an arbitrary noncomplete regular local ring with its maximal-adic topology.
notes: Known special cases and source distinction; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: Let $k$ be any field, let $z_1,z_2,\ldots$ be algebraically independent over $k$, and set \[ D=k[z_i^2,z_i^3\mid i\geq1]\subset k[z_i\mid i\geq1],\quad P_i=(z_i^2,z_i^3)D,\quad S=D\setminus\bigcup_{i\geq1}P_i,\quad R=S^{-1}D. \] Then $R$ is a one-dimensional noetherian domain. Its maximal ideals are precisely $\mathfrak m_i=S^{-1}P_i$, and \[ R_{\mathfrak m_i}\simeq L_i[z_i^2,z_i^3]_{(z_i^2,z_i^3)},\qquad L_i=\operatorname{Frac}\bigl(k[z_j^2,z_j^3\mid j\ne i]\bigr). \] Its regular locus is exactly $\{(0)\}$ and is not open.
notes: Proved: an explicit noetherian ring of infinitely many cusps; machine-extracted statement text; registry reconciliation ongoing

statement: For a flat map of noetherian rings $A\to B$, the locus of points whose local ring in the fibre is formally smooth over the residue field, for its maximal-ideal topology, need not be open. Explicitly, let $A=\mathbf F_p$ and let $B=R$ in Lemma~\ref{SA23-A-10} over $k=\mathbf F_p$. The locus is exactly $\{(0)\}$.

statement: Let $R$ be the explicit noetherian domain of Lemma~\ref{SA23-A-10} over $\mathbf F_p$. For its absolute Frobenius homomorphism $F_R:R\to R$, $a\mapsto a^p$, the flat locus in the target spectrum is exactly $\{(0)\}$. It is not open and contains no nonempty open subset.

statement: If $A\to B$ is of finite presentation and $A$ is noetherian, its flat locus in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is open. If additionally $B$ is flat over $A$, the locus of geometrically regular fibre points is the smooth locus and is open.
